input.question: Why do some people binge eat when they're stressed, while others lose their appetite entirely?
input.ground_truth: I'm gonna call the genetic variation card here. Eating while you're stressed makes sense for many reasons (additional energy may aid in alleviating the cause of the stress, plus the happiness of eating cancels out the unhappiness left by stress). However the inverse also has it's advantages (i.e, if you're in a sticky situation, thinking about eating may not be the most productive thing to do). Psychological factors may also be at play, including strength of will and how the specific person perceives eating.

Question: Why do some people binge eat when they're stressed, while others lose their appetite entirely?

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have two friends, Sam and Alex. When they feel really stressed, like before a big test or when they’re sad, they react differently with food.

**Sam** feels like eating a lot of snacks all at once. This is called "binge eating." When Sam is stressed, their body might feel like it needs comfort, so they eat to feel better for a little while.

**Alex**, on the other hand, doesn’t want to eat anything when stressed. Their tummy might feel funny or they just don’t feel hungry at all. Sometimes, stress can make Alex’s body forget about food.

So, people are different! Some eat more when stressed because food feels like a hug. Others don’t want to eat because stress makes them feel weird or not hungry. Both ways are normal, but different brains and bodies react in their own way.
